title: Replace the spatial-hash wall-clock gate with a deterministic complexity assertion
intent: Test-only fix. test_spatial_hash_with_real_data asserted `elapsed < 0.1`, which measures how fast the CI runner is rather than how the algorithm scales. It failed on PR #345 — a @supabase/supabase-js client bump that cannot touch Python code — at 0.604s. Replaced with a comparison-count assertion that tests the property actually worth protecting (deduplication does not regress to the O(n^2) linear scan the module replaced), plus a new test covering the collision path the sparse-random case never reaches. No production code changes.

diff_articulation.what_changed: test_spatial_hash_with_real_data is renamed to test_spatial_hash_does_not_degenerate_to_linear_scan and now counts is_close() calls instead of timing the loop. find_existing() calls is_close() exactly once per candidate in the 3x3 cell neighbourhood, so the call count is the work the structure does, and it is identical on every machine. A second test, test_spatial_hash_deduplicates_coincident_points, exercises the matching path. A shared _counting_point_class helper builds the instrumented PointLike.
diff_articulation.why_not_redundant: This is the only wall-clock assertion in the entire services/api test suite, so nothing else covers the performance claim and nothing else shares this failure mode. The replacement is strictly stronger: the old assertion could pass while the structure silently degraded on a fast runner, and could fail while it was perfectly healthy on a slow one.

commands_run: Root cause: PR #345 CI showed `FAILED tests/test_dxf_security_patch.py::TestSecurityPatchIntegration::test_spatial_hash_with_real_data - AssertionError: Spatial hash too slow: 0.604s / assert 0.604 < 0.1`, with `1 failed, 8785 passed`. The second red gate, Core CI Summary, is only the aggregator step `Fail if any core job failed` — two gates, one cause.

Attribution: PR #345 changes only packages/client/package.json and package-lock.json (@supabase/supabase-js 2.112.3 -> 2.112.4). There is no causal path from a client npm package to app/cam/spatial_hash.py. Sibling dependabot PRs #344, #346 and #348 pass API Tests on the same base.

Measured locally, 7 runs at n=1417: median 0.0055s, min 0.0050s, max 0.0218s against a 0.1s threshold — 18x of headroom. The 0.604s CI observation is ~110x the local median, which is runner contention, not an algorithmic change.

Measured the real work: at the default cell_size=0.1 over a 400x300mm area the structure makes 1 is_close() comparison for 1417 points, so wall-clock here is dominated by allocation and dict operations, not by the algorithm under test.

Confirmed the new gate is not vacuous by degrading cell_size and watching it trip: 0.1 -> 1 comparison (0.00/insert, PASS); 1.0 -> 79 (0.06, PASS); 10.0 -> 7127 (5.03, PASS); 100.0 -> 493411 (348.21, FAIL); 1000.0 -> 1003236 (708.00, FAIL, exactly the naive n(n-1)/2 linear scan). The 10*n bound sits with margin between healthy and degenerate.
grep -rln 'elapsed <|duration <|time.time() - start' services/api/tests/ -> only test_dxf_security_patch.py. This was the suite's sole timing-based gate.
py -3.11 -m pytest tests/test_dxf_security_patch.py -q --no-cov -> 24 passed (23 before; one test added)

files.intent: Replace a machine-speed assertion with a deterministic complexity assertion, and cover the deduplication path.

architecture_scan.acknowledgement_notes: Test-only change. No production code, no API, no schema, no dependency change. app/cam/spatial_hash.py is untouched — the implementation was never the defect.

no_backend_no_schema: No backend API, route, schema, persistence, workflow, or build change.
